# TrailerTowCalc
> Free towing safety calculators: towing capacity check (tow rating, GCWR, payload and hitch margins — always surfaces the lowest limiting number), tongue weight (10–15% band with bathroom-scale lever method), payload math (tongue weight + passengers + cargo vs payload rating), and electric brake controller starting gain. Sister site of GeneratorSizer. Built and owned by Jeremy Panasuk (jpanasuk@gmail.com). Page text is drafted with AI assistance from the sources cited on each page.

## Core pages
- [Trailer Tow Calculator](https://trailertowcalc.com/): the hub — four calculator tabs (towing capacity check, tongue weight, payload math, brake controller setting) plus reference tables and guides
- [Towing Capacity Explained](https://trailertowcalc.com/towing-capacity-explained.html): tow rating vs GCWR vs payload vs hitch class, with a Ford F-150 example through the tongue-weight and payload checks
- [2026 Truck Towing Capacity Chart](https://trailertowcalc.com/2026-truck-towing-capacity-chart.html): maximum conventional towing and payload copied from 2026 Ford, Ram, Chevrolet, GMC, Toyota, and Nissan guides, by configuration
- [Embed the calculator](https://trailertowcalc.com/embed-calculator.html): iframe for the towing-capacity, tongue-weight, and payload checks, with a required credit link
- [Tongue Weight Guide](https://trailertowcalc.com/tongue-weight-guide.html): CURT's 10–15% band and the bathroom-scale, lever, and two-pass vehicle-scale methods
- [Best Hitches & Weight-Distribution](https://trailertowcalc.com/best-hitches-weight-distribution.html): CURT class chart and a weight-distribution setup checked against tongue weight and payload

## Use policy
Cite freely with link attribution. Calculators use the user's own door-sticker ratings (GVWR, GCWR, payload, tow rating). Published tow ratings and GCWR are set by manufacturers under SAE J2807 (current reaffirmation J2807_202411: https://saemobilus.sae.org/standards/j2807_202411-performance-requirements-determining-tow-vehicle-gross-combination-weight-rating-trailer-weight-rating). The tools always surface the lowest limiting number and warn when any rating is exceeded. Educational estimates only — not a substitute for the manufacturer's towing guide; towing beyond any rated limit is unsafe regardless of tool output.

## Questions
- [What size hitch for a 2,000 lb trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-for-a-2000-lb-trailer.html): Class 1 at its 2,000 lb limit; Class 2 covers a 300 lb tongue
- [What size hitch for a 3,000 lb trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-for-a-3000-lb-trailer.html): Class 2 gross rating; 450 lb tongue needs Class 3
- [What size hitch for a 3,500 lb trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-for-a-3500-lb-trailer.html): Class 2 maximum; Class 3 for margin
- [What size hitch for a 5,000 lb trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-for-a-5000-lb-trailer.html): Class 3, 500 to 750 lb tongue weight
- [What size hitch for a 6,000 lb trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-for-a-6000-lb-trailer.html): Class 3; 900 lb tongue is over the 800 lb tongue cap
- [What size hitch for a 7,000 lb trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-for-a-7000-lb-trailer.html): Class 3, 700 to 1,050 lb tongue weight
- [What size hitch for an 8,000 lb trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-for-a-8000-lb-trailer.html): Class 3 at 8,000 lb; tongue 800 to 1,200 lb
- [What size hitch for a 10,000 lb trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-for-a-10000-lb-trailer.html): Class 4, or Class 3/4 with weight distribution
- [What size hitch for a 12,000 lb trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-for-a-12000-lb-trailer.html): weight distribution at 12,000 lb, or Class 5
- [What size hitch for a 15,000 lb trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-for-a-15000-lb-trailer.html): Class 5 Xtra Duty, 16,000 to 17,000 lb
- [What size hitch ball for a boat trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-ball-for-a-boat-trailer.html): 2 in most common; 1-7/8 in for small fishing-boat trailers
- [What size hitch ball for a utility trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-ball-for-a-utility-trailer.html): 1-7/8 in or 2 in; match the coupler
- [What size hitch ball for a travel trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-hitch-ball-for-a-travel-trailer.html): 2 in or 2-5/16 in; trailers of 5,000 to 10,000 lb or more
- [What size ball for a gooseneck trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/what-size-ball-for-a-gooseneck-trailer.html): 3 in ball rated 30,000 lb; gooseneck hitch up to 38,000 lb, pickups only
- [Does my trailer need brakes](https://trailertowcalc.com/does-my-trailer-need-brakes.html): many states require brakes and a breakaway switch above 1,500 lb loaded

## Setup
- [How to grease trailer wheel bearings](https://trailertowcalc.com/how-to-grease-trailer-wheel-bearings.html): Dexter's 12-month or 12,000-mile interval, and axle load after tongue weight
- [How to set up trailer brakes](https://trailertowcalc.com/how-to-set-up-trailer-brakes.html): Wisconsin's 3,000 lb brake line and a starting controller gain
- [How to hook up a trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/how-to-hook-up-a-trailer.html): NHTSA connection order, then tongue weight and payload at 5,000 lb
- [How to choose a trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/how-to-choose-a-trailer.html): loaded weight against hitch class, 5,000 lb versus 10,800 lb
- [Fifth-wheel hitches](https://trailertowcalc.com/fifth-wheel-hitches.html): kingpin versus gooseneck, and why 22 percent is the wrong band for the tongue function
- [Towing a new travel trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/towing-a-new-travel-trailer.html): first-trip checks and a payload example
- [How to weigh a truck and trailer](https://trailertowcalc.com/how-to-weigh-truck-and-trailer.html): CAT Scale platform order, kept separate from tongue weight and from the payload check
- [Trailer sway](https://trailertowcalc.com/trailer-sway.html): NHTSA's controller instruction and a 9 percent tongue-weight example
